claims.text: The unmodified Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy is a single-phase BCC alloy.
Asymmetric XRD peaks in the unmodified alloy indicate dendritic versus interdendritic compositional micro-segregation.
The unmodified alloy has significantly lower room-temperature fracture strain than theoretical expectations or compositionally similar systems.
Adding approximately 4 at.% Cr to Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr induces precipitation of a C15 Laves phase.
The Cr-induced C15 Laves phase has a volume fraction of approximately 4%.
The C15 Laves phase is a cubic AB2 phase.
Local atomic-size mismatch and electronegativity differences drive Laves-phase formation.
The Laves phase forms a reticulated interconnected network at interdendritic and grain boundaries.
The reticulated Laves network impedes crack extension by forcing crack deflection, branching, or bridging and by increasing crack-path tortuosity.
Crack-path modification by the Laves network increases fracture toughness and fracture strain.
Cr introduces significant lattice distortion into the BCC matrix because of atomic-size mismatch and electronegativity differences.
Cr-induced lattice distortion produces solid-solution hardening and increases yield strength through greater lattice friction.
Cr addition contracts the lattice parameter of the BCC matrix.
The BCC lattice parameter shifts from approximately 3.42 Å to below 3.39 Å after Cr addition.
Annealing near or above 900 °C can trigger C15 Laves-phase precipitation.
Laves-phase formation requires the relevant atomic-radius ratio in segregated regions to approach approximately 1.22.
The Cr concentration must remain below a threshold for complete transformation to a single Laves phase.
The Laves-phase volume fraction and morphology depend on cooling rate and local segregation kinetics.
The magnitude of BCC lattice contraction depends on the segregation profile of the base elements.

contradictions.description: The stated precipitation condition gives temperatures above 900 °C as the example, whereas the proposed test uses exactly 900 °C, so the experiment does not unambiguously satisfy its own stated thermal boundary.
